title: TWA 599
summary: A Fokker F-10 crashed shortly after takeoff from Kansas City on the first leg to Wichita, killing all eight aboard including Notre Dame football coach Knute Rockne. Moisture had entered the interior of one wooden wing over time, weakening the glue bonds connecting the wing structure. One spar failed, the wing developed uncontrolled flutter and separated from the aircraft. The crash brought about significant changes in airplane safety and forced the industry to adopt all-metal aircraft designs.
probable_cause: Structural failure of the wooden wing caused by moisture penetration that weakened the glue bonding the wing laminate.

factors.evidence: The wings of Fokker Trimotors were made of wood laminate vulnerable to moisture
moisture had entered the interior of one wing over a period but was not detected in-service
wooden aircraft design proved structurally vulnerable and forced the industry to adopt all-metal aircraft and advance design standards
One spar finally failed; the wing developed uncontrolled flutter and separated from the aircraft

events.text: The Transcontinental and Western Air scheduled flight was from Kansas City to Los Angeles with a stopover in Wichita on March 31, 1931.
The co-pilot's radio call to Wichita indicated the weather here is getting tough and the crew planned to turn around and go back to Kansas City.
The wooden wing became moist over time, causing the glue connecting the wing to the fuselage to weaken, allowing one spar to fail.
One spar finally failed and the wing developed uncontrolled flutter and separated from the aircraft near Bazaar, Kansas, killing all eight occupants.
